cards.text: Friend, Israel is at war with the Ammonites, and the people of Gilead just made Jephthah their leader and commander. He sent the Ammonite king a long message, and the king paid it no attention. Like a paragraph in the group chat that gets NOTHING back. Not even a thumbs up.

cards.question: Jephthah is about to move against the Ammonites. First, what comes upon him?

answers.text: A deep sleep from the LORD

cards.text: He passes through Gilead and Manasseh, then Mizpah of Gilead, and advances on the Ammonites. And he makes a vow to the LORD: "If indeed You will deliver the Ammonites into my hand,"

cards.question: Jephthah's vow is about the moment he gets back home. What does he say will belong to the LORD?

answers.text: Whatever comes out his door to greet him
The first lamb born in his flock
A tenth of what he takes in battle

cards.question: Jephthah vows to offer it up as a burnt offering.

cards.text: So Jephthah crosses over to fight the Ammonites. Now that big "if" in his vow is about to get its answer.

cards.question: In the fight, the Ammonites hold their ground against Jephthah.

cards.text: With a great blow he devastates twenty cities, and the Ammonites are subdued before the Israelites. Then Jephthah heads home to Mizpah, and the door of his house opens.

cards.question: Coming out the door to meet Jephthah, with tambourines and dancing, is his ___.
Jephthah has other children besides this daughter.

cards.text: The moment Jephthah sees her, he tears his clothes.

cards.question: Jephthah cries out, "No! Not my daughter!" Why does he say he can't take the vow back?

answers.text: He gave his word to the LORD
The elders of Gilead heard it
He swore it before his army

cards.text: Then his daughter answers him, "My father," and friend, what she says next takes my breath away.

cards.question: Jephthah's daughter tells him to ___ his word to the LORD, because the LORD has avenged him of the Ammonites.
Then Jephthah's daughter asks her father for one thing. What is it?

answers.text: Two months in the mountains with her friends
Two months at home with her father
Two months at Shiloh with the priests

cards.question: Up in the mountains with her friends, Jephthah's daughter goes to ___ her virginity.

cards.text: After two months, she returns to her father, and he does to her as he had vowed. She had never had relations with a man.

cards.question: After this, a custom starts in Israel. What is it?

answers.text: Young women go out yearly to lament her
Fathers stop making vows before a battle
Families dance with tambourines every spring

cards.text: Every year, the young women of Israel go out for four days to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite. This one's heavy, friend, and Jephthah's story isn't over yet.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Friend, Israel is at war... commander.' 'He sent the Ammonite king... no attention.' 'Like a paragraph in the group chat that gets NOTHING back.' 'Not even a thumbs up.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card cites Judges 11:11-28, but 'Israel is at war with the Ammonites' comes from Judges 11:4. The citation should start at the first verse the card uses, Judges 11:4-28.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question's setup line, 'Jephthah's vow is about the moment he gets back home,' rules out both wrong answers. The first lamb of his flock and a tenth of the battle spoils have nothing to do with arriving home, so the setup points straight to 'Whatever comes out his door to greet him.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The statement 'Jephthah vows to offer it up as a burnt offering' uses 'it' to point back to the previous card's answer, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what 'it' is, such as whatever comes out his door to greet him.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question 'After this, a custom starts in Israel' uses 'this' to point back to card 18, which is no longer on screen. The right answer, 'lament her,' never says who 'her' is. The question should name Jephthah's daughter and what happened.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The first sentence of card 20 repeats the custom the baker just answered on card 19 (the young women go out every year to lament Jephthah's daughter). It adds only 'four days' and 'the Gileadite.' Because card 19 already asks about the passage's last verse, card 20 can be just the line saying the story isn't over. Alternatively, the 'four days' detail can be moved to an earlier card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
